market_holds: XYF no longer trades on its fundamentals. On 2026-11-06 the CEO-affiliated controlling holder, Mangrove Coast Investment, which has about 93% of the votes, sent a non-binding going-private proposal at US$6.03 per ADS (13D: debt from third-party banks plus Mangrove equity or rollover). The stock went from 4.70 to 5.75 (+22%) that day and has since drifted to about 5.23 (Yahoo bars, 2026-11-25 intraday). That leaves a 15.3% spread to the offer, against a 28% premium over the pre-offer close. A special committee of three independent directors was formed on 2026-11-18 (6-K, 2026-11-19); no advisers are named and no timeline is given. There is no listed option chain, no sell-side EPS estimate (finviz shows none) and no quantitative Q3 guide: the Q2 release on 2026-08-24 dropped volume guidance and kept a 'conservative stance until improvement proves durable'. Q2 facilitation was RMB11.63bn, down 70% YoY, at the low end of the 11.5-12.5bn guide. Thin: about 100k ADS a day, short interest about 0.07m shares. Before the offer, prints moved it a lot (2025-11-21 -15.7%, 2026-03-26 -26.2%, 2026-05-27 +10.2%, 2026-08-24 +2.0%, own arithmetic on Yahoo bars), but that was a free-floating stock. Peers have fallen hard in November (QFIN -22% and FINV -19% from 11-02 to 11-25, including QFIN -9.5% and FINV -4.4% today on heavy volume around FINV's Q3, non-GAAP EPS -26% YoY). XYF is flat over the same stretch because it is held up by the bid.
view: This is a merger-arbitrage stock that happens to report. The price is the offer less a discount for deal risk: a Chinese controlling-holder take-private that needs third-party bank financing, in a sector whose earnings are collapsing under the 24% rate cap. Q3 results will almost certainly be weak year on year, since the Q3 2025 base was RMB33.6bn of volume. Sequentially they may look better as credit keeps improving, but with no consensus there is no beat or miss line, and the free float is not pricing earnings power anyway. What could move it inside a Friday half-day window that ends at the 13:00 close: (a) any wording on the proposal or the special committee (advisers retained, timeline), which is mildly positive; (b) a print bad enough that arbs fear a price cut or a financing problem, which is mildly negative. Neither is signalled by anything I found. The stock already gave back about 9% of the offer pop while peers fell 20%, so the spread is wide and has absorbed sector risk. I see no unpriced, directional reaction. I expect a small move, well inside the 5.44% deadband, with a slight downside lean from the sector tape and thin holiday liquidity.

recommendation.reason: The price is anchored to a $6.03 controlling-holder offer with a 15% spread, so the Q3 numbers move it only through deal-probability channels that nothing public points to. There is no consensus, no option market and no guide to beat. Peer weakness is visible and already sits in the wide spread. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The release or call announcing a buyer price cut or withdrawal, or an unexpected financing problem (down hard). Or the special committee naming advisers and starting negotiations alongside a clean credit print (a modest move toward the offer).

self_critique: Chinese controlling-holder take-privates often get repriced lower when the business deteriorates, and this one needs third-party bank debt in a sector that has fallen 20% this month. If Q3 shows a fresh credit relapse, arbs could widen the 15% spread sharply even on a holiday half-day, so the downside tail is fatter than my 3% size suggests. The other side: a 15% spread already discounts a lot, and an advisers-retained line could tighten it. I cannot tell which tail the release favours.
